A church window in a German town once showed a mysterious piper, and a date: June 26th, 1284. #ForgottenAndFound What the town's own oldest records actually say happened that day has nothing to do with rats (they weren't added to the story for another 275 years), and the real historical theory for what happened to those children is stranger than the fairy tale.

This video uses AI narration and AI-generated illustrations.

Sources: Wikipedia — "Pied Piper of Hamelin"; Museum Hameln (museumhameln.de) — official exhibition page on the competing historical theories; the Lüneburg manuscript (c. 1440–1450) and the Zimmern Chronicle (Froben Christoph von Zimmern, c. 1559–1565); linguist Jürgen Udolph's surname-based emigration research as reported via Museum Hameln and secondary historical coverage.

#ForgottenAndFound #PiedPiper #Hamelin #GermanFolklore #FolkloreWithAHistory
